_comment: Provenance for WASM bundles built from the pqctoday-hsm repo and vendored into this hub. When you rebuild a bundle with its hsm build script, update its `hsmCommit`/`builtAt`. Verify drift with `npm run sync:wasm:check` (compares against a sibling ../pqctoday-hsm checkout when present; no-op otherwise). Bundles built from other sources (openssl upstream, pqctoday-tpm) are intentionally omitted.

bundles.name: cacp-kmip
bundles._buildNote: Follow-up rebuild closing a 1-commit drift the CSD02 migration's own last hsm commit (cfd71fc, KAT provenance metadata) introduced against the prior entry (8e7b09c/2026-07-24) — found by running the provenance check with an explicit HSM_REPO_PATH override before shipping this release, since the default sibling-path check is a no-op without one. cfd71fc only touches kmip/kat/*.json documentation (no wasm-exported function signatures, no engine behavior), so this rebuild is a formality for the release record, not a functional change — confirmed via another real `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` + `wasm-bindgen` + live node smoke test (Query, Create, malformed-frame handling, ML-DSA-65 CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify round-trip, an unimplemented-algorithm rejection, and a full X25519MLKEM768 hybrid-KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round-trip — not simulated), from a clean worktree exactly matching `hsmCommit`. `sync:wasm:check:cacp-kmip --check` is clean after.

bundles.name: softhsmrustv3-engine
bundles._buildNote: PKCS#11 v3.2 Baseline Provider + generic pre-hash mechanisms (2026-07-17, hsm commit 644a839, landed directly on main): adds the CKO_PROFILE object (CKA_PROFILE_ID=CKP_BASELINE_PROVIDER, every Profiles v3.2 §5.1 requirement checked against the fetched spec) and implements the previously-unadvertised generic CKM_HASH_ML_DSA (0x1F) / CKM_HASH_SLH_DSA (0x34) pre-hash mechanisms (CK_HASH_SIGN_ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT.hash parsing, remapped onto the existing hash-specific mechanisms). `hsmCommit` above (5c0eadd) is a same-day follow-up that only refreshes hsm's own tracked rust/pkg_bundler/ build artifact + a wasm/Cargo.lock version bump — no rust/ source changed beyond 644a839. No new exported wasm functions — same API surface (.d.ts/.js text diffs are empty), only the .wasm binary changed; verified 302 Rust unit tests pass (0 failed) and the .wasm binaries are byte-identical across all three hub vendor copies (public/wasm/rust/, src/wasm/, src/vendor/softhsm-wasm/wasm/ — the last of which was found stale relative to the other two, predating the FrodoKEM/McEliece shadow-stack fix, and is now back in sync as a side effect of this rebuild). Prior entry (`5303bd3`, 2026-07-11): fixed the FrodoKEM/Classic-McEliece wasm32 shadow-stack overflow in Encapsulate — see hsm CHANGELOG.md for that history.

bundles.name: softhsm-cpp-engine
bundles._buildNote: Includes fix(cpp) 250994d: SP800-108 KDF now requires keyed-MAC PRF (CKM_SHA256_HMAC); bare hash IDs rejected per PKCS#11 v3.2 §6.42.

bundles.name: openssl-pkcs11
bundles._buildNote: PKCS#11 engine swapped from the C++ SoftHSMv3 fork to the pure-Rust softhsmrustv3 (hsm rust/, wasm32-unknown-emscripten staticlib). The C++ fork's only crypto backend is OpenSSL libcrypto -- the same libcrypto.a linked into this binary -- so the chain CLI -> pkcs11-provider -> C++ softhsm -> same libcrypto was circular. The Rust engine has no OpenSSL dependency (RustCrypto + patched fips204/205/ml-kem), making the provider path a genuinely independent implementation. Build flags: -sSTACK_SIZE=8MB (Emscripten's 64KB default overflows during ML-DSA/ML-KEM keygen and traps with 'memory access out of bounds'). pkcs11-provider config.h is now generated by scripts/gen-pkcs11-provider-config-h.sh rather than required to pre-exist, and defines DEFAULT_PKCS11_MODULE so the provider resolves the in-process engine with no config file. The apps_startup() provider-registration patch ('Fix A') is recovered into pqctoday-priv/openssl-wasm-patches/ after previously existing only inside a gitignored openssl source tree -- verified at parity with the shipped binary before this rebuild. Token-state persistence across openssl.wasm's per-command modules (-sEXIT_RUNTIME=1) uses a NEW mechanism: a genuine C atexit() hook (registered in this hub's own src/wasm/cms_provider_init.c) calls a new Rust export, pqctoday_hsm_atexit_stash, which writes engine state to a fixed MEMFS path; JS reads it back via a pure FS.readFile after callMain returns. This replaced an earlier design that assumed OpenSSL's own provider teardown (C_Finalize) would run during callMain's atexit chain -- verified directly that it does not: OPENSSL_cleanup() runs on every callMain but never unloads a provider loaded via an explicit OSSL_PROVIDER_load() call, which is how this embedding registers pkcs11. ML-KEM keys now carry CKA_ENCAPSULATE/CKA_DECAPSULATE per PKCS#11 v3.2 SS6.68.2 (previously CKA_DERIVE, which is wrong for KEM keys). Token-init decisions now query the token's own CKF_TOKEN_INITIALIZED flag (C_GetTokenInfo, newly exported) rather than inferring from JS-side bookkeeping alone, per PKCS#11 v3.2 SS5.5.7. Verified end-to-end in Node against this exact binary: provider loads reporting the Rust engine; C_InitToken/InitPIN/GenerateKeyPair(ML-DSA-65 and ML-KEM-768) succeed; a real ML-KEM-768 encapsulate/decapsulate round trip across a fresh module produces byte-identical shared secrets; a 4-step CMS workshop flow (keygen -> self-signed cert -> cms sign -> cms verify), each step in its OWN fresh module, round-trips a real payload correctly using only the file-based snapshot handoff. Pinned anchor KATs (ML-DSA-44/65/87, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s, ML-KEM-512/768/1024 decap, bit-flip negatives) pass against this binary. NOT YET VERIFIED: a full pass in an actual browser (all proof above is Node-against-the-binary); a possible second lost OpenSSL source patch referenced by the build script's own banner comment ('HRR detection') has not been confirmed present or absent.
